thesis: The hedge did its job - DBC is +2.7% while the book fell - and today's CPI showed exactly why, with gasoline up 3.9% driving over a third of the monthly increase. But the score has come off from +0.70 to +0.50 and oil fell on Friday, so the momentum that made it a 55-day breakout is fading. Keep it as the hedge; the case for adding at RSI 70 is no better than it was at RSI 76.
bull_case: This is the position the inflation data vindicates. August CPI put gasoline up 3.9%, accounting for over a third of the monthly increase - the commodity complex is not just correlated with the inflation problem, it is causing it. The supply disruption remains: US forces destroyed five Iranian tankers this week, Houthi militants struck Saudi energy facilities, and the EIA does not expect Middle East production to normalise until early 2027. DBC is +2.7% for us in a week the book fell, with ATR of just 1.5%, so the diversification is cheap. Packet still shows close > SMA50 > SMA200 with 63d momentum +14.9%.
bear_case: The momentum is rolling over: score +0.70 to +0.50 in a day, RSI down from 78 to 70, and oil prices fell on Friday even as equities rallied. The forecast problem is the same one and it has not improved - the EIA has Brent averaging about $85/b in 3Q26 and J.P. Morgan $86/$80/$78 through year end, against spot near $101. A hiking Fed that succeeds in killing demand is bearish commodities, so the hedge is not unconditional: the same event that makes us want the hedge can unwind it. And the ceasefire gap risk is permanent - Brent went $105 on 23 July to $69 on 2 July on headlines alone, in both directions.
catalysts: Hormuz transit volumes and further strikes
Qatar/China-brokered talks on reopening the Strait
15-16 Sep 2026 FOMC and the demand outlook
risks: Score +0.70 to +0.50 and RSI 78 to 70: momentum fading
EIA and J.P. Morgan both forecast Brent well below spot
A hiking Fed killing demand unwinds the hedge
Ceasefire headline gap risk that no stop covers
invalidation: Unchanged from 8 Sep: the hedge thesis fails on a daily close below 31.20, which breaks the SMA50. A confirmed US-Iran ceasefire invalidates it immediately regardless of price. Worth adding only on a pullback toward 31.20 that holds, not at the high.
